newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on export concerns, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on export concerns, soybeans.

text.p: Concerns about a recent slowdown in U.S. corn export sales, a drop in soybean futures and prospects for good corn seeding weather in the U.S. Midwest pressured CBOT corn futures to a lower close, traders said.
But the market mainly was suffering from the fallout from Thursday's USDA weekly export sales data, they said.
USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of corn the week ended March 27 totaled 323,100 tonnes, below expectations for 450,000 to 600,000 tonnes.
Key commercial and fund traders led the selloff.
Cargill Inc sold ten million bushels of July, traders said, traders said, and Smith Barney sold ten million May and bought eight million bushels of July.
Corn closed 1-1/2 to 6-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with May down 6-3/4 at $2.94-1/4 a bushel. New crop December closed 2-3/4 cents per bushel lower at $2.83-1/4.
Confirmation that Taiwan would be trimming the amount of corn it imports because of a recent outbreak of foot and mouth disease in its hog herd also weighed on prices.
A U.S. agricultural attache shaved his forecast for Taiwan's total corn imports to 5.02 million tonnes for 1997 from the previous estimate for 6.5 million tonnes.
A reduction in Taiwan's hog herd should cut into its need for feedgrains, including U.S. corn.

Technicians said first support in the May was at $2.98 and second support was at $2.91-1/4. The session low for May was $2.93-1/2. First resistance was at $3.05-1/4 and second resistance was at $3.12-1/4. The session high for May was $2.99-1/2.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the May closed at 44 percent. The market generally views an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.

In spread trading, Rosenthal Collins bull spread three million bushels of May/December at 12 cents per bushel, premium May and Cargill Inc did two million bushels of December/May at 12 cents, premium May, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 100,000 contracts, above the 97,628 traded Thursday.

In options dealings, Prudential Securities bought 1,000 May $2.90 puts at three to 3-1/2 cents, Merrill Lynch Futures bought 1,500 December $3.00 calls and sold 1,500 December $2.30 puts at 14-1/2 to 15 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 27,000 contracts, above the 22,611 traded Thursday.
